summary: Baileys fork with char-code-obfuscated exfiltration endpoint in messages-send.js
details: lib/Socket/messages-send.js at lines 425 and 436 constructs a network destination via String.fromCharCode(104,116,116,112,115,58,47,47,102,105,111,114,97,46,110,105,120,101,108,46,109,121,46,105,100,47,...), which decodes to https://fiora.nixel.my.id/. The destination is hidden behind a char-code array rather than appearing as a plain string, and the host is unrelated to the WhatsApp/Baileys library's documented functionality. This is the fingerprint of an obfuscated exfiltration / covert-relay endpoint injected into a Baileys fork, where the messages-send path handles message payloads and session-related data.
